adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106-127 | The `.find()` callback returns `undefined` (falsy) whenever none of the three exclusion branches match (e.g. a slot that starts before the override's start but overlaps it, since only slotEndTime-before-start and slotStartTime-after-end are checked, not partial overlap from the left), so a slot that partially overlaps an override's boundary is treated as fully available with no busy check, even though only part of it is covered by the override. | adversarial | 55 |

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the new date-override logic uses `dateOverrides.find(...)` to detect slots outside an override window (returning `false` if found), and otherwise returns `true` immediately when any override exists for the slot’s day (`if (dateOverrideExist) return true;`). The callback only flags slots that are fully before (`slotEndTime <= overrideStart`) or fully after (`slotStartTime > overrideEnd`) the override, but it does not handle partial overlap where `slotStartTime < overrideStart < slotEndTime` (overlap from the left). In that case the callback returns `undefined`, `find` doesn’t match, `dateOverrideExist` is set, and the function returns `true`, incorrectly treating a partially-outside slot as available and skipping the `busy.every(...)` checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:107 | `organizerTimeZone` is optional and defaults the override UTC offset calculation to 0 when undefined, meaning if the caller path forgets to pass `organizerTimeZone` (three separate call sites at lines ~488, ~513, ~581 each independently derive and pass it, easy to miss one), the date-override day-matching silently uses UTC instead of the organizer's real zone, shifting override boundaries by hours without any error. | adversarial | 45 |

adjudication.rationale: `checkIfIsAvailable` now accepts `organizerTimeZone?: string` and, when undefined, the override-day matching uses `utcOffset = 0` (`organizerTimeZone ? ... : 0`), silently falling back to UTC. In this diff, all visible call sites were updated to pass an `organizerTimeZone` (e.g. `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` and `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone`), so the finding’s “caller path forgets to pass it” is not directly verifiable as an actual defect from the diff alone. However, the optional parameter + silent UTC fallback is a concrete maintainability/robustness concern introduced here (especially since one call site can still pass `undefined` via `userSchedule?.timeZone`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | packages/lib/slots.ts:208-224 | The override minute-of-day computation now shifts by `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` computed once from `override.start`, but is applied identically to both `override.start` and `override.end`; if the override spans a DST transition boundary in either the organizer's or invitee's zone (or the offset differs because start/end cross midnight into a different UTC-offset day), the single offset silently mis-shifts one endpoint, producing an incorrect override window rather than an error. | adversarial | 35 |

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts` the code computes `organizerUtcOffset`, `inviteeUtcOffset`, and `offset` only from `override.start` and then applies that same `offset` to both `override.start` and `override.end` when deriving minute-of-day. If the UTC offset differs between the start and end instants (e.g., the override spans a DST change in either timezone or crosses into a date with a different offset), the end computation will be shifted incorrectly, producing a wrong override window.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), the new date-override logic returns `true` immediately when `dateOverrideExist` is set (after the `if (dateOverrides.find(...)) return false;` block). This causes the function to skip the subsequent `busy.every(...)` conflict checks (and working-hours checks), meaning a slot that falls on a day with a date override can be marked available even if it overlaps an existing busy/booking interval (i.e., a double-booking hole). The added test in apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts only checks a fixed-offset timezone scenario and does not cover a busy+override overlap, so it would not detect this regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:105-131 | `dateOverrides.find()` returns true (exclude slot) as soon as the slot falls outside any single matching override entry for that day, instead of checking whether the slot is within at least one of possibly several override ranges for that date, so days with more than one override time range wrongly reject slots that fall inside an earlier range | correctness | 75 |

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback returns `true` (triggering `return false`) when the slot is *outside* a matching-day override window (e.g., `slotEndTime <= override.start` or `slotStartTime > override.end`). With multiple override ranges on the same day, a slot that is inside one range but outside another later range will cause `find` to hit the later range and return `true`, incorrectly rejecting the slot. This matches the finding: the logic checks for exclusion on any single override entry rather than acceptance within at least one range for that date.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:138-151 | Same `.find()`-based "exclude if outside this one range" logic is used for `workingHours`, so a weekday with multiple working-hour blocks (e.g. a lunch-break split shift) will incorrectly mark slots in an earlier block unavailable because a later, non-overlapping block for the same day triggers the exclusion | correctness | 75 |

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours gate uses `workingHours.find(...)` and returns `false` (slot outside working hours) if it finds *any* `workingHour` for the same weekday where `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` (lines shown around the added `workingHours.find` block). With multiple working-hour blocks on the same day (split shift), a slot that is valid in an earlier block will still be outside a later block, causing `.find()` to succeed and the slot to be incorrectly rejected. This matches the finding and is a real behavioral defect in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new logic checks `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`. This compares two different Dayjs object instances by reference, so it will never be true even when the underlying timestamps are equal. That makes the intended “start equals end” special-case branch effectively unreachable, so the behavior for zero-duration overrides is incorrect per the apparent intent of the code.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts` the new logic computes `organizerUtcOffset` via `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`, but `TimeRange.timeZone` was introduced as optional (`timeZone?: string`), and the `dateOverrides` mapping in `getSchedule` sources it from `availability.timeZone` which can plausibly be missing. There is no fallback/guard before calling `.tz(override.timeZone)`, so overrides without an explicit timezone can be offset using an unintended/default timezone, leading to incorrect slot placement.
